serve: Treat serve as a transition, not a single visual pose.
Best serve evidence is: players reset/aligned, most bodies relatively still, server starts motion, receiver/reacting player starts moving immediately after.
A person standing with a paddle is not enough; require reset-to-rally context.
If the camera is blocked at the exact contact, infer only from surrounding reset and immediate rally, otherwise omit.
Audio can support a candidate when a paddle/ball hit appears near the reset-to-rally transition, but audio alone must not create a serve.
Huanchaco Pt3 trusted final shows many valid points begin after a clear short reset, not necessarily a long stationary pause.
For Huanchaco-style clips, keep the serve candidate only when it can be paired with a plausible rally and later stop; do not add extra serves inside that rally.
For user-marked or model-candidate serve moments, search tightly around that second; the true serve is often near the indicated second, not necessarily exactly on the sampled frame.
When a candidate second has reset posture and immediate rally start, prefer a mark close to that second rather than drifting several seconds away.
end: Final is often easier than serve: players stop chasing, posture relaxes, they walk back or align again.
If the rally continues after a candidate final, reject the final.
Huanchaco Pt3 trusted final reinforces that point end often appears as immediate body relaxation/walking after the last return, even if the ball is hard to see.
Do not require repeated/static frames for point end; repeated frames are rare and should not be the main signal.
A point can be determined when players stop running with intensity, relax, walk away, or leave the active court area because the ball went too far/out.
If players are no longer chasing the ball and no one remains actively playing the rally, infer that the point ended earlier even if the exact ball exit is hard to see.
paddle_highlight: Raised paddle/highlight requires a deliberate signal held around 2 seconds.
A player or body blocking the camera is not a highlight.
Normal horizontal paddle during play is not enough unless held deliberately as a signal.
camera_framing: Higher camera angle can reduce blocks, but must not lose seated people or the court context.
The model should tolerate occasional blocks by using before/after context.
negative_examples: Use negatives explicitly: otra_cosa without Fin de punto usually means not a serve, even if motion/stance looked tempting.
Do not train contradictory entries where decision says saque but note says Fin de punto; keep them for human review only.
Basura means ignore for serve/end training unless a separate final note is later confirmed.

strict_rules: Do not label a serve from motion alone.
A serve candidate requires a reset posture: players relatively still, server separated enough to initiate, then the rally starts immediately after.
Do not mark the same rally with multiple serve starts unless the previous point has a confirmed end.
Do not label a final from motion alone.
A final candidate requires the rally to visibly stop: players stop chasing/running, paddle collision/acknowledgement, ball dead, or clear reset before the next serve.
A hit is not a point boundary; it is only an internal action marker.
Local-motion scenes are hints only. They must not become final serve/end pairs unless supported by a serve-to-end pattern.
If uncertain, omit the mark instead of inventing it. It is faster for the human to add a missing mark than delete many false marks.
Paddle highlight is valid only when the paddle is deliberately held/signaled for about 2 seconds, not when normal play or body obstruction hides the camera.
Any annotation after 08:00 in youtube_1oNOWqOeE64-human-final.json must be ignored.
Human final 240726 Pt3 confirms that long dead or unclear stretches should be labeled trash/ignored instead of forcing serve/end pairs.
When a corrected clip has many trash marks, prefer conservative omission over dense invented rallies.
Use Huanchaco Pt3 as trusted cadence reference for Huanchaco Pt4: prefer one serve followed by one final per continuous rally.
Do not split a continuous Huanchaco rally into multiple points unless players visibly reset or acknowledge the end.
Huanchaco Pt4 final confirms render scenes should use the latest corrected serve before each final when multiple serves appear before the same end.
For final output, derive clips from human mark pairs rather than stale automatic scene spans when they disagree.
For endings, prioritize loss of player intensity and court disengagement over frame repetition.
When players stop chasing or leave the play area after a far/out ball, mark the final near the decisive stop, not at the next visible reset.
For serves, stay close to the indicated/candidate second unless surrounding context clearly proves a later or earlier serve.
